questions.question: Rani Machaiah is an Ummathat folk dancer from ___________________ who received Padma Shri 2023 in the field of Art (Folk Dance).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rani Machaiah is renowned for her contributions to the Ummathat folk dance, a traditional dance form of Karnataka.
 
• She was honored with the Padma Shri award in 2023 for her excellence in the field of Art, specifically Folk Dance.
 
• The Padma Shri is one of the highest civilian awards in India, recognizing distinguished contributions in various spheres.
 
• Ummathat is a significant cultural dance of the Kodava community, performed by women to the beats of traditional drums and cymbals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Padma Awards**:

 
 
• The Padma Awards, including Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Vibhushan, are among the highest civilian honors in India.
 
• These awards are announced annually on the eve of Republic Day, recognizing individuals for their contributions in various fields such as arts, education, industry, literature, science, sports, medicine, social service, and public affairs.
 
• The Padma Shri is the fourth highest civilian award in the Padma series, following the Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan, and Padma Bhushan.
 
 
 
• **Kodava Community**:
 
 
• The Kodavas are an ethno-linguistic group from the Kodagu district of Karnataka, known for their distinct culture and traditions.
 
• They have a rich heritage of martial traditions and are known for their unique festivals, dances, and cuisine.
 
• Ummathat is one of the traditional folk dances performed by Kodava women, showcasing their cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Folk Dances of Karnataka**:
 
 
• Karnataka has a rich tradition of folk dances, including Yakshagana, Dollu Kunitha, and Veeragase.
 
• These dances are characterized by vibrant costumes, dynamic movements, and traditional music, reflecting the cultural diversity of the state.
 
• Folk dances in Karnataka often depict historical, mythological, and social themes.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Musical Instruments**:
 
 
• Ummathat and other folk dances are often accompanied by traditional musical instruments like the 'Dudi' (drum) and cymbals.
 
• These instruments play a crucial role in setting the rhythm and enhancing the overall performance.
 
• The use of traditional instruments is an integral part of preserving and promoting the cultural heritage of Karnataka.

questions.question: Which of the given colours in NOT associated with the judo grades?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pink**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Judo belt colors** generally include white, yellow, orange, green, blue, brown, and black.
 
• The color **pink** is not traditionally associated with judo grades.
 
• Judo belts signify the rank and expertise level of the practitioner, with **white** being the beginner level and **black** representing advanced proficiency.
 
• Some variations in belt colors can exist between different judo organizations, but pink is not a standard color.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judo Grading System:**

 
 
• The judo ranking system is based on the Kyu-Dan system, where Kyu grades are for colored belts and Dan grades are for black belts.
 
• Each color indicates the level of knowledge and proficiency in judo techniques.
 
 
 
• **Origin of Judo:**
 
 
• Judo was created by Jigoro Kano in Japan in 1882.
 
• Kano developed judo as a physical, mental, and moral pedagogy in the form of a martial art.
 
 
 
• **Judo in the Olympics:**
 
 
• Judo was first included as an Olympic sport in the 1964 Tokyo Olympics.
 
• It is a globally practiced sport with significant international competitions.
 
 
 
• **Judo Techniques:**
 
 
• Judo techniques are classified into throwing techniques (nage-waza) and grappling techniques (katame-waza).
 
• Mastery of these techniques is essential for advancement in judo ranks.

questions.question: According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023, which of the following states showed the fastest poverty reduction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Uttar Pradesh** has shown the fastest reduction in poverty according to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023.
 
• The state has significantly reduced its poverty rate from 37.79% in 2015-16 to 22.93% in 2019-21.
 
• The efforts include extensive implementation of social welfare programs and schemes aimed at improving the living conditions of the poor.
 
• Uttar Pradesh's performance is attributed to improvements in education, health, and living standards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):**

 
 
• The MPI is a measure designed to capture the multidimensional nature of poverty, beyond income alone, by considering factors like health, education, and living standards.
 
• The index is developed by the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
 
 
• **Poverty Reduction Initiatives:**
 
 
• Various government schemes like Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, and the National Health Mission have contributed to poverty reduction.
 
• Focus on improving infrastructure, job creation, and access to basic amenities have been key strategies.
 
 
 
• **Education and Health Improvements:**
 
 
• Increased access to education and healthcare services has been pivotal in reducing poverty in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Programs like Mid-Day Meal Scheme and Ayushman Bharat have had a significant impact.
 
 
 
• **Living Standards:**
 
 
• Improvements in living standards, such as better housing, sanitation, and electricity access, have played a crucial role.
 
• Initiatives like Saubhagya Scheme (for electricity) have improved the quality of life for many.

questions.question: Which of the following goals of the Five-Year Plan is directly related to the people?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Equity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Equity** in the context of the Five-Year Plans refers to reducing inequality in income and wealth distribution.
 
• It involves providing all citizens with equal opportunities to improve their living standards.
 
• Equity aims at social justice by focusing on the welfare of the poor and marginalized sections of society.
 
• Key measures include land reforms, progressive taxation, and social welfare programs to support vulnerable groups.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Growth:**

 
 
• Focuses on increasing the country's economic output and overall development.
 
• Targets sectors like agriculture, industry, and services to boost GDP.
 
 
 
• **Modernisation:**
 
 
• Refers to adopting new technologies and methods to improve productivity and efficiency.
 
• Includes initiatives in infrastructure development, education, and healthcare.
 
 
 
• **Self-reliance:**
 
 
• Aims to reduce dependence on foreign aid and imports.
 
• Encourages indigenous production and utilization of local resources.
 
 
 
• **Five-Year Plans:**
 
 
• Were central planning mechanisms for economic and social development in India.
 
• Formulated by the Planning Commission from 1951 to 2017 before it was replaced by NITI Aayog.

questions.question: What was a key focus of the First Five Year Plan (1951-1956)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agricultural development**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The First Five Year Plan (1951-1956) of India primarily focused on the development of the agricultural sector.
 
• The plan aimed to address the food deficit and improve agricultural productivity to ensure food security for the growing population.
 
• Substantial investments were made in irrigation projects, land reclamation, and community development programs.
 
• Emphasis was placed on the expansion of agricultural infrastructure and the use of modern farming techniques to increase crop yields.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five Year Plans:**

 
 
• India's Five Year Plans were centralized and integrated national economic programs.
 
• The Planning Commission of India was responsible for formulating these plans, which aimed to achieve specific economic goals over five-year periods.
 
 
 
• **Green Revolution:**
 
 
• The Green Revolution occurred in India during the late 1960s and 1970s, significantly increasing agricultural production through high-yield variety seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation.
 
• This revolution was a response to the need for food security and was influenced by the agricultural focus of the First Five Year Plan.
 
 
 
• **Irrigation Projects:**
 
 
• Large-scale irrigation projects such as the Bhakra Nangal Dam and Hirakud Dam were initiated during the First Five Year Plan.
 
• These projects aimed to provide a reliable water supply for agriculture, thereby increasing crop productivity.
 
 
 
• **Community Development Programs:**
 
 
• The plan included community development programs to promote rural development and enhance the quality of life in villages.
 
• These programs focused on education, health, sanitation, and infrastructure development.

questions.question: Padma Shri awardee Shovana Narayan is associated with which Indian classical dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Shovana Narayan is a renowned Indian classical dancer known for her expertise in Kathak.
 
• She has been honored with the prestigious Padma Shri award for her contributions to the field of dance.
 
• Shovana Narayan has performed extensively both in India and internationally, promoting Kathak on global platforms.
 
• Her style is characterized by its intricate footwork, graceful movements, and expressive storytelling.
 
• She has also trained numerous students, contributing to the preservation and propagation of Kathak.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak**:

 
 
• Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.
 
• It originated from the northern regions of India and is known for its intricate footwork and spins.
 
• Kathak dancers use a combination of hand gestures, facial expressions, and body movements to narrate stories.
 
• The dance form is traditionally performed to classical Hindustani music.
 
 
 
• **Padma Shri**:
 
 
• Padma Shri is the fourth highest civilian award in the Republic of India.
 
• It is awarded to citizens of India in recognition of their distinguished contributions in various spheres such as arts, education, industry, literature, science, sports, medicine, social service, and public affairs.
 
• The award is announced on Republic Day (26th January) every year.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Dance**:
 
 
• India has a rich tradition of classical dance forms that include Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Odissi, and Sattriya.
 
• Each dance form has its own unique style, costumes, and music.
 
• These dances are deeply rooted in Indian mythology, spirituality, and cultural traditions.
 
 
 
• **Storytelling in Kathak**:
 
 
• Kathak dancers often narrate tales from Indian epics like Mahabharata and Ramayana.
 
• The dance form originally evolved from the storytelling practices of ancient bards known as Kathakars.
 
• These narratives are enhanced through the dancer's expressions, gestures, and rhythmic footwork.

questions.question: Which of the following Vedas is primarily the collection of magic spells and charms to ward off evil spirits and diseases?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atharvaveda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Atharvaveda** is one of the four Vedas of ancient Indian scriptures.
 
• It is primarily a collection of **magic spells and charms** intended to ward off evil spirits and diseases.
 
• The Atharvaveda contains hymns, mantras, and incantations for various purposes, including healing and protection.
 
• It is distinct from the other three Vedas (Rigveda, Yajurveda, and Samaveda) due to its focus on practical aspects of daily life and rituals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rigveda**

 
 
• The oldest of the four Vedas, primarily consisting of hymns and praises dedicated to various deities.
 
• It is divided into ten books called Mandalas.
 
 
 
• **Yajurveda**
 
 
• Focuses on the procedures for performing various rituals and sacrifices.
 
• It is divided into two parts: the Shukla (White) Yajurveda and the Krishna (Black) Yajurveda.
 
 
 
• **Samaveda**
 
 
• Consists mainly of melodies and chants intended to be sung during rituals.
 
• It is often considered the root of Indian classical music.
 
 
 
• **Vedic Literature**
 
 
• The Vedas are the oldest sacred texts of Hinduism, composed in early Sanskrit.
 
• They form the foundation of Vedic traditions and are divided into four main categories: Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda, and Atharvaveda.

questions.question: Which chemical is used for whitening (or removal of colours) of cloth in cloth industries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcium oxychloride**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Calcium oxychloride**, commonly known as bleaching powder, is extensively used in the textile industry for bleaching cloth.
 
• Its strong oxidizing properties help in the effective removal of colors and stains from fabrics.
 
• Bleaching powder is preferred due to its cost-effectiveness and efficiency in large-scale applications.
 
• It also serves a dual purpose by disinfecting the cloth during the bleaching process.
 
• Calcium oxychloride is a stable compound that releases chlorine gradually, ensuring consistent bleaching action.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bleaching Powder (Calcium oxychloride)**:

 
 
• Chemical Formula: Ca(OCl)₂
 
• It is produced by reacting calcium hydroxide with chlorine gas.
 
• It is widely used for bleaching, disinfecting water, and sanitation purposes.
 
• It is a white or grayish powder with a strong chlorine smell.
 
 
 
• **Other Chemicals Used in Textile Industry**:
 
 
• **Sodium Carbonate (Na₂CO₃)**: Used in the dyeing process to fix dye on fibers.
 
• **Sodium Hydrogencarbonate (NaHCO₃)**: Used for neutralizing acids in textile processing.
 
• **Calcium Chloride (CaCl₂)**: Used as a desiccant and in dyeing baths to remove moisture.
 
 
 
• **Textile Bleaching**:
 
 
• Bleaching is a chemical process that removes natural colors from fibers to achieve whiteness.
 
• Common bleaching agents include chlorine-based compounds, hydrogen peroxide, and sulfur dioxide.
 
• Effective bleaching ensures uniform dyeing and enhances fabric appearance.
 
 
 
• **Safety Considerations**:
 
 
• Bleaching agents can be hazardous and should be handled with care, using proper protective equipment.
 
• Proper ventilation is necessary to avoid inhalation of chlorine fumes during the bleaching process.
 
• Storage of bleaching agents should be in a cool, dry place, away from direct sunlight and incompatible substances.

questions.question: Which Five-Year Plan was the first to be terminated before its completion, and why?

options.text: Second Plan, due to economic instability
Seventh Plan, due to political conflicts
Fifth Plan, due to a change in government
Third Plan, due to natural disasters

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fifth Plan, due to a change in government**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-1978) was the first plan to be terminated prematurely.
 
• This plan was terminated by the newly elected Janata Party government in 1978.
 
• The termination occurred due to the government's shift in economic policy direction.
 
• The Janata Party government replaced the Fifth Plan with a Rolling Plan for 1978-1980.
 
• The Rolling Plan aimed to provide more flexibility in planning and adjustment to changing economic conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans in India**:

 
 
• India's Five-Year Plans were centralized and integrated national economic programs.
 
• These plans were developed, executed, and monitored by the Planning Commission of India.
 
• The first Five-Year Plan was launched in 1951 and focused on the agricultural sector.
 
 
 
• **Planning Commission**:
 
 
• The Planning Commission was an institution in the Government of India, which formulated India's Five-Year Plans.
 
• It was established in March 1950 by a resolution of the Government of India.
 
• It was replaced by the NITI Aayog in January 2015.
 
 
 
• **Janata Party**:
 
 
• The Janata Party was formed in 1977 as a coalition of several opposition parties.
 
• It was the first non-Congress party to form a government at the center after the 1977 general elections.
 
• The government was led by Prime Minister Morarji Desai.
 
 
 
• **Economic Policy Shifts**:
 
 
• The Janata Party government focused on reducing government intervention in the economy.
 
• They aimed to promote a more market-oriented economic policy.
 
• This shift led to the termination of the ongoing Fifth Five-Year Plan.

questions.question: Nilgiri is one of the oldest mountain ranges, located at the tri-junction of which three states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Nilgiri mountain range is located at the tri-junction of the states of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka in southern India.
 
• It is part of the Western Ghats, a mountain range that runs parallel to the western coast of the Indian peninsula.
 
• The Nilgiri Hills are known for their rich biodiversity and are home to several protected areas and wildlife sanctuaries.
 
• The highest peak in the Nilgiri range is Doddabetta, which stands at an elevation of 2,637 meters (8,652 feet).
 
• The Nilgiris are famous for their tea plantations, which produce some of the finest tea in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Western Ghats:**

 
 
• The Western Ghats is a mountain range that runs parallel to the western coast of the Indian peninsula, spanning six states: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is recognized as one of the world's eight "hottest hotspots" of biological diversity.
 
• The Western Ghats are home to a large number of endemic species of flora and fauna.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity in the Nilgiris:**
 
 
• The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, established in 1986, includes the Nilgiri Hills and is part of the Western Ghats.
 
• It is home to several endangered species, including the Nilgiri tahr, Bengal tiger, Indian elephant, and lion-tailed macaque.
 
 
 
• **Tea Plantations:**
 
 
• The Nilgiri Hills are known for their extensive tea plantations, which are a major source of income and employment in the region.
 
• Tea from the Nilgiris is known for its distinct flavor and aroma, and the region produces both black and green tea.
 
 
 
• **Climate:**
 
 
• The Nilgiri Hills have a subtropical highland climate, characterized by mild temperatures and high humidity.
 
• The region experiences heavy rainfall during the monsoon season, contributing to its lush green landscapes.

questions.question: Who was the British Prime Minister when India gained independence in 1947?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Clement Attlee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Clement Attlee was the British Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951.
 
• He led the Labour Party to victory in the 1945 general election, replacing Winston Churchill.
 
• Under Attlee's leadership, the British government decided to grant independence to India.
 
• The Indian Independence Act was passed on July 18, 1947, and India gained independence on August 15, 1947.
 
• Attlee's government also oversaw the partition of India, leading to the creation of Pakistan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Independence Act 1947**:

 
 
• This act was passed by the British Parliament and led to the partition of British India into two independent dominions, India and Pakistan.
 
• It marked the end of British rule in India and the transfer of power to Indian leaders.
 
 
 
• **Mountbatten Plan**:
 
 
• Also known as the June 3rd Plan, it was the plan for the partition of India proposed by the last Viceroy of India, Lord Louis Mountbatten.
 
• It outlined the method of partition and was accepted by the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League.
 
 
 
• **Partition of India**:
 
 
• The partition resulted in the creation of two independent dominions, India and Pakistan.
 
• It led to significant demographic shifts, with large-scale migrations and communal violence.
 
 
 
• **Labour Government Reforms**:
 
 
• Under Attlee, the Labour government implemented significant reforms including the establishment of the National Health Service (NHS) and the nationalization of key industries.
 
• These reforms laid the foundations for the modern welfare state in the UK.

questions.question: In which state is the festival of ‘Kalinga Mahotsav ’celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Kalinga Mahotsav is celebrated in Odisha, particularly at the Dhauli hills, near Bhubaneswar.
 
• This festival commemorates the Kalinga War fought by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BC.
 
• It is a major festival that showcases the rich cultural heritage and martial arts traditions of Odisha.
 
• The event features a variety of performances, including traditional dance forms like Odissi and other classical Indian dances.
 
• The festival aims to promote peace and non-violence, reflecting the transformation of Emperor Ashoka after the Kalinga War.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Emperor Ashoka**

 
 
• He was the third emperor of the Maurya Dynasty and ruled from 268 to 232 BCE.
 
• After witnessing the mass deaths during the Kalinga War, Ashoka embraced Buddhism and promoted non-violence and Dharma (moral law).
 
• Ashoka's reign is marked by the spread of Buddhism across Asia.
 
 
 
• **Dhauli Hills**
 
 
• Dhauli Hills are located on the banks of the Daya River in Odisha.
 
• The site is famous for the Shanti Stupa (Peace Pagoda) built by the Japan Buddha Sangha and the Kalinga Nippon Buddha Sangha.
 
• It is believed to be the battlefield of the Kalinga War.
 
 
 
• **Odissi Dance**
 
 
• Odissi is one of the classical dance forms of India, originating from the state of Odisha.
 
• It is known for its intricate movements, gestures, and expressions.
 
• Odissi dance is deeply rooted in the traditions and culture of Odisha, often depicting themes from Hindu mythology.
 
 
 
• **Martial Arts of Odisha**
 
 
• Odisha has a rich tradition of martial arts, including the Paika Akhada, which is a form of ancient martial art.
 
• Paika Akhada was historically performed by the warrior class known as Paikas.
 
• This martial art form includes various physical exercises and fighting techniques.

questions.question: With which sport is the Indian Para Athlete Parul Parmar associated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Badminton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Parul Parmar is a prominent Indian Para Athlete known for her achievements in **badminton**.
 
• She has won several medals at international events, including the **Asian Para Games** and the **World Para-Badminton Championships**.
 
• Parul Parmar has been a significant figure in promoting badminton among differently-abled athletes in India.
 
• She has been awarded the **Arjuna Award** for her contributions to the sport of badminton.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Para-Badminton:**

 
 
• Para-badminton is a variant of badminton designed for athletes with physical disabilities.
 
• The sport is governed by the Badminton World Federation (BWF).
 
• Para-badminton was included in the Paralympic Games for the first time at the **Tokyo 2020 Paralympic Games**.
 
 
 
• **Arjuna Award:**
 
 
• The Arjuna Award is one of the highest sporting honors in India.
 
• It is awarded annually by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to recognize outstanding achievement in sports.
 
• The award includes a bronze statue of Arjuna, a certificate, and a cash prize.
 
 
 
• **Asian Para Games:**
 
 
• The Asian Para Games are a multi-sport event held every four years for athletes with physical disabilities.
 
• The event is organized by the Asian Paralympic Committee (APC).
 
• The first Asian Para Games were held in Guangzhou, China, in 2010.
 
 
 
• **World Para-Badminton Championships:**
 
 
• The World Para-Badminton Championships is an international competition for para-badminton players organized by the BWF.
 
• The event features various categories based on the type and level of disability.
 
• It serves as an important platform for athletes to compete at the highest level and showcase their skills.

questions.question: Which of the following is the state religion of Bangladesh, as per the Constitution of Bangladesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Islam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the Constitution of Bangladesh, Islam is the state religion.
 
• Article 2A of the Constitution explicitly mentions Islam as the state religion.
 
• While Islam is the state religion, the Constitution ensures equal status and equal rights in the practice of other religions.
 
• Bangladesh is a secular state in practice, promoting religious harmony and coexistence among different religious communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Secularism in Bangladesh:**

 
 
• Secularism was one of the original four principles of the 1972 Constitution of Bangladesh.
 
• The principle was removed during military rule but was reinstated in the Constitution through the 15th Amendment in 2011.
 
 
 
• **Religious Demographics:**
 
 
• Islam is the religion of about 90% of the population in Bangladesh.
 
• Hinduism is the second-largest religion, followed by Buddhism and Christianity.
 
 
 
• **Freedom of Religion:**
 
 
• The Constitution guarantees freedom of religion and permits religious practices of all communities.
 
• There are legal protections against religious discrimination.
 
 
 
• **Religious Festivals:**
 
 
• Major Islamic festivals like Eid-ul-Fitr and Eid-ul-Adha are national holidays.
 
• Other religious communities also celebrate their festivals, such as Durga Puja for Hindus and Christmas for Christians.

questions.question: The Constitution (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Orders (Amendment) Bill, 2024 intends to modify the list of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Constitution (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Orders (Amendment) Bill, 2024 aims to update the list of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes specifically for the state of Odisha.
 
• This bill seeks to include new communities and make adjustments to the existing lists to ensure accurate representation.
 
• The amendment is crucial for providing the benefits of reservation, education, and employment opportunities to the newly included communities.
 
• The process of modifying the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes lists is governed by Article 341 and 342 of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scheduled Castes (SCs)**

 
 
• Scheduled Castes are communities that are historically disadvantaged and were subjected to untouchability in India.
 
• The Constitution provides for affirmative action in the form of reservations in education, employment, and political representation.
 
• Article 341 of the Indian Constitution allows the President to specify the castes, races, or tribes deemed to be Scheduled Castes.
 
 
 
• **Scheduled Tribes (STs)**
 
 
• Scheduled Tribes are indigenous communities recognized as socially and economically disadvantaged.
 
• Article 342 of the Indian Constitution allows the President to specify the tribes or tribal communities deemed to be Scheduled Tribes.
 
• The Constitution mandates affirmative action for STs similar to SCs, including reservations in various sectors.
 
 
 
• **Article 341 and 342**
 
 
• Article 341 pertains to the identification of Scheduled Castes, while Article 342 deals with the identification of Scheduled Tribes.
 
• Both articles empower the President to notify these communities, and any subsequent changes require a parliamentary amendment.
 
• These articles are fundamental in ensuring that the benefits of affirmative action reach the intended communities.
 
 
 
• **Affirmative Action**
 
 
• Affirmative action in India includes a system of reservations for SCs, STs, and Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in education, employment, and political representation.
 
• The goal is to address historical injustices and provide equal opportunities to disadvantaged communities.
 
• Reservations are a contentious issue, often debated in terms of their impact on meritocracy and social equity.

questions.question: Who among the following has the power to dissolve the legislative assembly of a state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor of the State**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Governor of a state in India has the constitutional power to dissolve the legislative assembly of the state.
 
• This action can be taken based on the advice of the Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers.
 
• Such a dissolution usually happens when the Chief Minister loses the majority support in the assembly.
 
• The Governor exercises this power under Article 174(2)(b) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The dissolution is aimed at paving the way for fresh elections and is a significant step in the democratic process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 174 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• Article 174 empowers the Governor to summon and prorogue the state legislature and to dissolve the legislative assembly.
 
• The Governor acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Governor:**
 
 
• The Governor acts as the nominal head of the state with the real powers being vested in the Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers.
 
• The Governor's role includes appointing the Chief Minister, dissolving the legislative assembly, and giving assent to bills passed by the state legislature.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Assembly Dissolution:**
 
 
• Dissolution of the legislative assembly can be either automatic at the end of its five-year term or earlier upon the recommendation of the Chief Minister.
 
• The dissolution leads to the requirement of new elections to form a new assembly.
 
 
 
• **Emergency Situations:**
 
 
• In case of constitutional breakdown, the President of India can dissolve the state legislative assembly and impose President's Rule under Article 356.
 
• This is done on the recommendation of the Governor when the state government is unable to function as per the Constitution.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first music director to bring Rock 'n' Roll to Hindi tunes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rahul Dev Burman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rahul Dev Burman**, also known as R.D. Burman, was a pioneering music director in the Hindi film industry.
 
• He is credited with bringing **Rock 'n' Roll** to Hindi film music during the 1960s and 1970s.
 
• His innovative compositions incorporated western musical styles, including rock, jazz, and disco, into Indian cinema.
 
• R.D. Burman's work on films like **"Teesri Manzil" (1966)** is particularly noted for its rock 'n' roll influence.
 
• He collaborated extensively with prominent singers like Kishore Kumar and Asha Bhosle, further popularizing the fusion of western and Indian music styles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rock 'n' Roll:**

 
 
• A genre of popular music that originated in the United States in the late 1940s and early 1950s.
 
• Characterized by a strong rhythm, simple melodies, and the use of electric guitars, it was a significant influence on many other music genres.
 
 
 
• **Hindi Film Industry (Bollywood):**
 
 
• The Hindi-language film industry based in Mumbai, India, and one of the largest centers of film production in the world.
 
• Known for its diverse array of musical styles incorporated into film soundtracks.
 
 
 
• **Innovations in Music:**
 
 
• R.D. Burman was known for his experimental approach, combining various musical elements to create unique soundscapes.
 
• He was one of the first Indian composers to use electronic instruments and multi-track recording.
 
 
 
• **Collaborations with Singers:**
 
 
• His collaborations with Kishore Kumar resulted in some of the most memorable songs in Hindi cinema.
 
• He married Asha Bhosle, who sang many of his compositions, further enhancing his musical legacy.

questions.question: Which of the following rights is considered a component of the Right to Life and Personal Liberty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Privacy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Right to Privacy is considered a component of the Right to Life and Personal Liberty under Article 21 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This recognition was affirmed by the Supreme Court of India in the landmark judgment of Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) vs Union of India in 2017.
 
• The judgment held that the Right to Privacy is a fundamental right and an intrinsic part of the freedoms guaranteed by the Constitution.
 
• Privacy encompasses various aspects including personal autonomy, bodily integrity, and the protection of personal information.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 21 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• Article 21 states that "No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to the procedure established by law."
 
• This article is fundamental to the protection of individual rights in India.
 
 
 
• **Justice K.S. Puttaswamy vs Union of India (2017):**
 
 
• This case addressed the constitutionality of the Aadhaar project and the broader implications on privacy.
 
• The Supreme Court's verdict affirmed privacy as a fundamental right under the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Implications of the Right to Privacy:**
 
 
• It impacts various domains such as data protection, surveillance, and personal autonomy.
 
• Legislations and policies now need to ensure they do not infringe upon this fundamental right.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Many international human rights instruments, including the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, recognize the right to privacy.
 
• This right is crucial in the digital age where personal data is extensively used and shared.

questions.question: In June 2024, who resigned from their Wayanad Lok Sabha seat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rahul Gandhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rahul Gandhi** is a prominent Indian politician and a member of the Indian National Congress (INC).
 
• He represented the Wayanad Lok Sabha constituency in Kerala.
 
• In June 2024, Rahul Gandhi resigned from his Wayanad Lok Sabha seat.
 
• This resignation was a significant political event, drawing substantial media attention.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rahul Gandhi's Political Career**

 
 
• He is the son of former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and Congress leader Sonia Gandhi.
 
• He has served as the President of the Indian National Congress from December 2017 to August 2019.
 
• He has been a Member of Parliament for Amethi, Uttar Pradesh, before contesting from Wayanad.
 
 
 
• **Wayanad Constituency**
 
 
• Wayanad is a Lok Sabha constituency in Kerala.
 
• It is known for its high literacy rates and political engagement.
 
• The constituency has a diverse population with significant tribal communities.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress (INC)**
 
 
• One of the two major political parties in India, the other being the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
 
• Founded in 1885, it played a significant role in the Indian independence movement.
 
• The party advocates for a secular, democratic, and inclusive India.
